event: Day 38, before dawn: Hadley readies his pack with three days of provisions.
'I will be back by Day 40. Probably Day 39 if the ridgeline is clear.'
Wren hands him the letter; he tucks it into the waterproof pocket without looking.
Hadley notes the ghost-elm shimmer now reaches twenty meters past its Day 32 line.
'The Holding changed the range. Not just the settlement. The trees.'
'Count on the way.' 'I always count.' He gives the Rimfolk sign for 'I will be back.'
Hadley walks north through the ghost-elm perimeter; the settlement is four.
Brecca stands at the hall's north wall with her hands at her sides, not working.
Wren watches from the fire pit and does not go over.
Brecca lays her palm on the wall, flinches, and pulls it back.
'It is loud. Three hundred years of hands, all talking at once.'
Wren goes to her: 'What does it sound like?' 'Not sound. Weight.'
Her own work is a thin warm top layer, the healer's beneath, the builders heaviest of all.
Wren says that is the [Foundation Stone] signature, felt as weight instead of vibration.
'How long did it take you to stand it?' 'Thirty-six days.'
Brecca puts her hand back and holds, jaw set, without flinching.
'Start with the top layer. Your work.' Brecca's shoulders loosen a degree.
'I can feel my thumbprints in the joints.' 'That is [Pressed Intention].'
'It named it. It did not explain it. Show me what you see.'
Wren lays Detail Notation beside Brecca's hand: the intention layer is clearer than yesterday.
Wren calls Brecca's signature fragile, then corrects herself: 'Young.'
Brecca feels Wren's mark as a window, giving the stone more vocabulary.
The builders' layer is not heavy but certain: they never checked, they knew.
'I have been listening for three weeks.' 'That is three weeks more than yesterday.'
Late morning Wren finds Theron waist-deep in the eastern channel.
The east branch runs thirty meters, turns south, and changes to older coursed rubble.
It widens into a basin ending in a half-buried stone-lined cistern.
The cap is a fitted dressed stone with a thumb-width hole lined by a stone collar.
It stored rain from the settlement's drainage; his grandmother never mentioned a cistern.
'Because this was in the gap.' Theron reads the collar's craft with his thumb.
Dressed stone shows under the soil past the cistern: the channel goes on south.
Wren reaches through the bond; the signal is faint at this distance.
She pushes for detail and hits the limit of Journeyman Surveying: frosted glass.
She stops pushing and stays with what she cannot read, listening to the frost.
[Keen Survey] unlocks, waiting since Level 5 for her to need it.
She activates it: water table four meters, three-layer limestone like the threshold stone.
At the edge of its range she finds a second cistern south, in corrupted ground.
A discovery logs the eastern water infrastructure: +64 XP, 2111 / 2573.
'There is a second cistern. South.' A hundred and fifty to two hundred meters.
'We will need more than one degree.' 'Yes.'
'The next pulse is seventeen days.' 'Sixteen now.' Theron nods: a decision made.
Brecca has stood two hours at the north wall, learning to hear her own work.
In the afternoon Maret, packed and waiting, gathers them at the fire pit.
'The carried stone stays. My grandmother carried it sixty years so it could come home.'
She gives Theron her counting rod; she will cut a new one.
To Brecca: 'When the walls teach you what you do not understand, walk north.'
Brecca nods without speaking.
To Wren: the builders called this place not the Thornwild but the Vael.
Vael means 'the place that sings': before the corruption, the land itself sang.
Wren writes the word in her journal.
Said at the threshold stone during dawn, the stone may answer differently. 'You will find out.'
Maret touches Theron's cheek for three seconds; he closes his eyes.
Maret walks north without turning or waving, up the escarpment trail.
Wren watches until she is a shape on the ridge, and then just the ridge.
The evening fire is three; Theron sits in Maret's place, hand on her rod.
Brecca keeps her palms on the hall wall, no longer overwhelmed, practicing.
Wren journals Hadley's departure, the shimmer's reach, Keen Survey, the cistern network.
She writes of Maret's gifts: the rod, the name Vael, Brecca's instruction, the stone left.
The drift is one day; sixteen days to the third pulse. 'Three tomorrow.'
The fire burns down; the stone sings in the dark and three people hold the settlement.
